title: Army transfer money arrows erase the original's signed over-cap purse pullback
body:
Found during the owner-requested restrictions audit at released4d70275a. [ArmyDialogModels.cs](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/blob/4d70275aac4e155c0370a3ee23525cf34450a908/godot/UI/Dialogs/ArmyDialogModels.cs#L308) computes MaxMoneyToPartner and MaxMoneyBack with an outer Math.Max(0,...), then AdjustMoney clamps a net amount between those nonnegative capacities. A nominal transfer into an over-cap purse does nothing instead of sending the excess back.

The [promoted purse-writes report row4](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/865755e04f107afc38cdb496669d882e2551aca6/docs/reports/2026-10-05-army-purse-writes-and-the-1000-cap.md) reads TArmyToArmy_ChangeMoney 0x442448 (:44044–44088): step=min(10 or100, min(1000-receiver,giver)), with NO floor at zero; giver-=step, receiver+=step on working copies. It explicitly says a receiver above1000 produces a negative step. Row4 and Split money arrows were not pressed in play, so this report supports a code-derived discrepancy, not fresh runtime parity.

Native production-model probe (exit0): two adjacent own armies, A purse100, B purse1100. ArmyTransferModel.ForArmies(A,B,classical-faithful); AdjustMoney(+100); ComposeOk() returns null. Original reported signed rule gives step -100: A200, B1000. Over1000 purses are legitimate (joins/capture can create them); this is separate from owner-approved saturation at32767.

Related [#757](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/issues/757) fixed treasury-to-purse signed pullback, not this ArmyTransferModel floor. Current [ArmyTransferCommand](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/blob/4d70275aac4e155c0370a3ee23525cf34450a908/src/IC2.Engine/Armies/Commands/ArmyTransferCommand.cs#L45) cites min(step,1000-receiver,giver), so its claimed rule and UI disagree.

Triage: bounded fidelity correction; no fix/release scheduled by audit. Preserve editable live previews, source/target identities and Cancel semantics. Test both arrow directions, over-cap receivers, repeated presses and split/shared model callers. An unchanged OK behavior is a separate research question; do not silently fold it into this fix.
